To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the incidence of vulvar SCC in Dutch women has been stable for the last 25 years; 2) the 5-year survival rate of vulvar SCC patients is still low, but has improved significantly in the last 25 years; and 3) patients with vulvar SCC have an increased risk of developing a subsequent primary cancer.
the incidence of vulvar cancer is increasing, and that the 5-year survival of women with vulvar cancer has improved.
the incidence of vulvar squamous-cell carcinoma (VSCC) has increased over time and that the survival rate has increased as well.

the incidence, mortality and survival of vulvar squamous carcinoma in The Netherlands and the role of the human papillomavirus (HPV) in the development of this cancer.
